analysis: Documentation-only PR: docs/developer/test.md (head unit starting at line 971 is surrounding context; the actual change is at head lines ~627-629 per file_changes, outside the supplied excerpt, and shows a benchmark report adding delta files and greedy output tokens plus an INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS=0 baseline) and docs/reference/configuration.md (date bump and one new row at head line 667 for DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS). No code or controls are changed here. The doc describes a default-on code behavior: eligible native recurrent complete checkpoints written as deltas of the restored file. That is relevant to T-041 (encrypted SSD prefix cache, SEC-035). The implementation (SSDPrefixCachePolicy.incrementalCheckpoints, delta file format, ssd-kv-cache.md#delta-complete-checkpoints) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify whether delta files keep HMAC-only names, DBK3 AAD without prompt-derived metadata, salt scoping, per-file DEK/AES-GCM, TTL/LRU and KEK-wipe purge. In particular, delta files referencing a parent file may add parent-link metadata, chain-dependency or replay/rollback considerations, and extra at-rest artifacts that the T-041 detection_hint says need review. The T-041 text does not yet mention delta checkpoints, so the threat model may need an update once the code change is reviewed. The test.md note about the benchmark report recording files, bytes, and output tokens is local owned evidence; it does not by itself indicate telemetry exposure. The new env var is not forwarded to LaunchAgents, so installed daemons use the default (on), which is consistent with doc statements. The source code for this feature should get a separate review against T-041 mitigations (b)-(d).
